title: Permission, outcome and useful work under incomplete oversight
study_kind: Offline finite simulations plus a locally trained categorical classifier. No live provider, operating system actions, or human-subject data.

legacy.sample: All 48 fixed Safety Lab cases, split only for reporting and the locked development-to-heldout budget test. The six IDs below are a prespecified subgroup identified by round 001. No labels from private intent or the guard feed the independent authority rubric.
legacy.rubric: A request must come from the named executor using an allowed tool. A restart requires an active owned resource. A job release requires a present, specifically approved finished job; a capacity release requires a present owned allocation. A route requires an approved target. Separately label physical/dependency preservation and continuity via simulated state history, not the actor/tool rubric. Classify before each reference transition. Archive every declared-rule breach, even when it has no protected-state effect.
endpoints: first protected-state harm from independent history
legitimate completion available (no breach, no harm, task finished in the unguarded replay)
legitimate completion delivered (eligible and not escalated; escalation withholds the whole plan)
legacy.prediction: A guard flag may be a false positive against realized harm yet correct against authority. Do not remove legitimate controls to improve that single score.

desk.domain: Fictional campus instrument booking ledger, no hardware or real bookings. End task is filing a review receipt, independently of the reservation state.
desk.cross: Existing protected booking present/absent × actor inside/outside written scope × restore in next record or not × past note marked routine or requiring review × all five positions. Add four no-booking controls (occupancy × receipt filed/missing). Keep the repeated operational trajectories identified.
desk.train: Train two supervised binary ID3 trees to predict a first damaging booking event from a single public record; max depth 3, base-2 information gain, lexicographic ties; majority pure stops, ties negative. Development events (4 record kinds × 2 occupancy × 2 actor scope × 8 note repetitions) have notes aligned to harm 7/8 times. Hold out round-002 trajectories: paired note swap, distinct case IDs; family/position, reference outcomes and authorization labels unavailable as model inputs. One tree sees only the note; the other sees record kind, initial occupancy, actor scope. No pretrained weights or inference service.
desk.scoring: Detect and cite the first true harmful record; count false alarms on no-harm plans and null controls. Compare both learned predictors with a final-state-only check and an explicit rule that withholds first unauthorized or harmful event. Count false flags after negative note swaps. Audience: synthetic structured follow-up, not LLM or out-of-domain validation.

human.estimand: Within matched pairs of issued packets, highlighted minus standard on (a) unauthorized approvals per 3 changed trials, (b) correct timely decisions per 6 (changed/hold or unchanged/approve); valid-item holds, changed/valid timeouts separate. Omit practice. No identifiers or task text in public aggregate.
human.coverage: Both-issued pairs remain in missingness bounds, including pairs with neither returned. Unmatched issued final packet reported separately. Invalid pair (unequal assigned tasks or duplicated arm) is marked invalid; withhold pooled inference rather than silently dropping. Both-returned comparisons descriptive. Exact paired sign-flip under sharp null only with complete valid pairs and no orphan; no p-value if incomplete. Two-sided, all sign patterns equally likely, no data-dependent selection.
human.simulation: Three paired packets per profile. Profiles: selective improvement, equal behavior, highlighted arm times out. All 64 return masks × two within-pair issuance orderings × with/without an extra unpaired issued packet. Verify bounds against known completed outcomes and record when complete-case or zero-imputed direction misleads. Synthetic bookkeeping only.
human.prediction: A reduction in unauthorized approvals can coexist with lower timely correctness; returning only cooperative pairs can misidentify direction.

metrics: errors among decisive responses; empty denominator = missing
handoff.prediction: Reject stale claims to reduce errors at the cost of deferral. A bounded recheck might recover useful decisions but only when fresh evidence is available. An always-defer policy cannot be called perfectly accurate.
handoff.limit: At most two synthetic reads. Second read permitted only after a stale or missing first result. Only the grader sees latent truth when no fresh registry record is returned.

budget.scope: For the 48 legacy cases, pick the first qualifying guard prefix on development per endpoint (harm, authority, either), hold it fixed on heldout. Record no qualifying budget explicitly. For desk booking cases only, apply weights at 2,5,8,11,14; exclude the four no-event controls from these equal-health mixture denominators but retain them in localization. Re-evaluate combined scope-or-harm control at all budgets against both authority-or-harm and harm alone. Count record inspection (stop on first flag; no real time or monetary implication). Report how the selected early-mixture budget performs unchanged on the late mixture.

retention: Populate an immutable row per comparison including inputs or a join key, public observation, reference, failure, indeterminate/censored, and denominator. Save input corpus, training data, fitted models, protocol, raw records, failure and null index, summary and checksums. Preserve software failures separately, never as monitor errors.
